title: Hurricane
description: Use this list before hurricane season and again when a Hurricane Watch is issued for your area.

sources.title: Winter Storms Aren't Over: CPSC Warns of Deadly Carbon Monoxide Risks and Fires During Power Outages

items.text: Look up your evacuation zone with county emergency management and your storm surge risk on NHC surge maps - water causes most hurricane deaths
Decide where you will go if told to leave (inland friend, hotel, or shelter) and plan a main and backup route
If you live in a mobile home, RV, or temporary structure, plan to leave for any hurricane
Run any generator outdoors only, at least 20 feet (6 m) from windows, doors, and vents - never in a garage or on a porch - and install battery CO alarms
Store at least 1 gallon (3.8 L) of water per person per day - several days minimum, 2 weeks if you plan to stay
Stock at least 2 weeks of non-perishable food that needs no cooking, plus a manual can opener
Refill prescriptions at the Watch stage and keep extra supply as your plan allows, with a written medicine list
Install hurricane shutters or have pre-cut plywood marked for each window - do not rely on taping windows
Choose your wind shelter spot: a safe room or a small interior windowless room on the lowest floor that will not flood
Program a battery NOAA Weather Radio with your county SAME code and turn on phone alerts
Put IDs, insurance, and medical records in a waterproof bag, and keep encrypted digital copies
Fill vehicle gas tanks when a Watch is issued - fuel lines and shortages build fast before landfall
Get cash in small bills at the Watch stage - ATMs and card readers fail without power
Bring in or tie down outdoor furniture, grills, trash cans, and other loose items that wind can throw
Fill bathtubs and large containers with water for flushing and cleaning (a bathtub water-storage liner keeps it cleaner for drinking)
Charge phones, power banks, and spare batteries before the storm
Check and restock the first aid kit
Pack pet food, carriers, leashes, records, and pet medicines - take pets with you if you evacuate
Store generator fuel safely outside the living space in approved cans, with fuel stabilizer for longer storage
Know where your gas, water, and main electrical shutoffs are and how to use them
Write emergency contacts on paper - do not rely only on your phone
Photograph your home and valuables for insurance before the storm
Buy flood insurance months ahead - homeowner's policies usually exclude flooding and NFIP policies take about 30 days to start
Clear gutters and drains and trim weak or dead tree limbs before the season
